the trap — why the noise ladder is not a robustness read

The no-SIGReg arm looks 76% more noise-robust. It is not — σ is absolute and its z is 18× larger.

training.eval_noise_sigmas is a fixed list [0.32, 0.55, 0.82] added to z. Per element, the control's z has RMS √1.12 = 1.06 and the no-SIGReg arm's has √343.7 = 18.5. The same σ is a 77.5% perturbation on one arm and a 4.4% perturbation on the other.

This matters for the flow. Flow matching mixes z with N(0, I) noise. A code at RMS 18.5 per element sits ~18× above the noise the flow prior assumes, so the signal-to-noise schedule the flow trains under is not the one it was designed for. Slide 12 measures it.

the trap, measured — why the token-space losses cannot rank this pair

Teacher-forced losses flatter the SIGReg-0 flow. At z RMS ~16, unit noise hides almost nothing.

LossFeat decodes the teacher-forced x_pred at a random t. The SIGReg-0 flow sits 16% above its ceiling from ep 0; the SIGReg-0.02 flow sits 171% above. Slide 7 predicted this: the ep-30 tokenizer's z has RMS √262 = 16.2, so N(0, I) noise is a ~6% perturbation and most t are already solved.

the answer — question 23

Recon is about the same without SIGReg, but z is unbounded. The flow without SIGReg mostly predicts the last context frame.

1
Reconstruction: SIGReg and no SIGReg perform very similarly. No SIGReg is slightly better, a very small gap: LossRecon 0.0227 / 0.0164 vs 0.0254 / 0.0181 at ep 72 (KITTI / nuScenes).
2
But no SIGReg does not bound the z scale. ZRowMeanSquare 344 vs 1.12 at ep 72, still climbing (slide 5).
3
Flow matching without SIGReg mostly predicts the last context frame. Only 2 frames are forecast, so predicting the last frame is competitive, and this accidentally gives the best performance (slides 11 and 15–19).
not measured
  • One seed per arm, tokenizer and flow.
  • Tokenizer epoch 30 vs 70 is not separated from SIGReg.

  • 128 Waymo windows only. No FD-OccAny, no held-out flow set.
